```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (PROPOSED; its §2.2 puts submission download out of scope, and O2–O3 here supersede that by your partner's progression), specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (Proposed).
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). A uv workspace of four package scaffolds: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest. No platform chosen; the ADR's Azure proposal is not accepted.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small. About 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, which is minutes of downloading at 3 requests/s (basis: SEC full-index and daily-index directories). Measured by Stage 1. |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large. Millions of files and weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/s (basis: index row count × request rate; not yet measured). Measured by Stage 2. |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk. Measured by Stage 3. |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). Stages 1–3 follow your partner's order. Stages 4–6 are the later hardening stages that the earlier stages' `Leaves out` fields point to.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index core
      Objective: Load real quarterly and daily master index files into one queryable filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: the filing-index table, its location and columns; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: One real quarter's quarterly master index and at least one real daily master index are in one table. Its row count is reported, and a filing listed in both files appears once. The findings record elapsed time, bytes downloaded, request count and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: full 1993–present range, raw-snapshot retention and replay, versioned per-quarter publication, quarterly reconciliation and withdrawals, daily catch-up after missed runs, historical-format fixtures → Stage 4; scheduling, deployment, monitoring → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions download
      Objective: Download the submissions named by a bounded real slice of index rows.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1 filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on disk for the slice, with their locations; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: Every submission named by one real daily index's rows is on disk or listed as failed with a reason. The findings record elapsed time, bytes, request count and rate, and a full-history estimate extrapolated from them.
      Leaves out: full-history download, resumable progress at scale → Stage 5; scheduling, deployment, monitoring → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2 submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents and a listing of the filings they came from; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: Each 10-K and 8-K among Stage 2's submissions has its main document extracted or is listed with a failure reason. Counts are reported, and the findings record elapsed time and data volume.
      Leaves out: extraction over the full history → Stage 5; scheduling, deployment, monitoring → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index hardening
      Objective: Make the filing-index table cover the full range and make it replayable and correction-safe (background spec §4.2–4.6 as input).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1 table and findings
      Produces: the full-range filing-index table with retained raw index files and versioned publication
      Exit: The full requested quarterly range is loaded, with any gaps listed. A rebuild from retained raw files, made with no SEC requests, reproduces the same table. A simulated missed day is caught up. A changed quarterly snapshot publishes its additions and holds its removals until approved.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment, monitoring → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Full-history submissions and extraction
      Objective: Download the submissions for the full requested range and extract 10-K and 8-K main documents across it.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 4 full-range table; Stage 2 findings (rate and estimate); Stage 3 extraction
      Produces: the full-range submissions and extracted documents, with a list of gaps
      Exit: Every submission in the requested range is on disk or listed as failed. An interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files. Extraction covers every 10-K and 8-K on disk. Total elapsed time and volume are recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment, monitoring → Stage 6
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Scheduled operation
      Objective: Run daily index, submission and 10-K/8-K ingestion on a schedule on a chosen platform, with monitoring and runbooks (the background ADR proposes Azure; the choice is still open).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4 and 5 outputs
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports and alerts
      Exit: Consecutive scheduled daily runs have been observed and each one has a run report. A failed run raises an alert. The runbooks cover catch-up and rollback.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O3). Each outcome gets a verdict with evidence: the implementing stage and plan, any Deviation notes, and any deferred_items entries. Each unmet outcome then exits one of two ways: a new stage, or a conscious deferral with a written why.
```

---

Wrote `specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md` with six stages in your order: index core, submissions, 10-K/8-K, then index hardening, full-history scale and scheduled operation. Approve the partition, or amend it, before I hand off Stage 1?
